Rate Card (A), Risk (C), and Cost (D) are not Benefit Plan offset type options. The offset type determines when the benefit plan begins relative to the project dates.

questions.stem: Which field, referenced from the cost plan, determines if a cost plan is Capex or Opex?
questions.explanation: The Cost type field (resource_type) (C) referenced from the cost plan determines if a cost plan is CAPEX or OPEX. Per the docs: 'cost_type - view financials by cost types such as Hardware Opex, External labor Capex, Software Capex, Software Opex.' The cost type classifies labor and non-labor costs as capital or operational. Resource category (A), currency type (B), and resource plan reference (D) do not determine CAPEX/OPEX classification.

questions.stem: You can forecast future costs of projects based on (Choose two.)

options.text: Changes in project such as project requirements

questions.explanation: Future costs of projects can be forecasted based on actual cost incurred (A) and changes in project requirements (B). Per the docs: 'forecast the future costs of projects and portfolios based on the actual cost and changed project requirements.' Incident cost (C) and paired instances (D) are not inputs to project cost forecasting.

questions.stem: To integrate Investment Funding with PPM, what plugin must be activated?
questions.explanation: To integrate Investment Funding with PPM, the Investment Funding for PPM plugin (A) — com.snc.investment_planning_pmo — must be activated. Per the docs: 'Verify that the Investment Funding for PPM (com.snc.investment_planning_pmo) plugin is activated. This plugin needs to be activated only when you want to retrieve the target amount for a portfolio.' The base Investment Funding (B) and Financial Planning (C) plugins are separate from the PPM-specific variant.

questions.stem: A customer needs to know what activity type is associated to time entries in the project so that they can capitalize build tasks. What is the best method to do this?

options.text: Leverage project time categories to classify the time.
Create a capital protect task flag.
Put all capital project tasks in one phase and report from those tasks.

questions.explanation: The best method to associate activity types with time entries for capitalizing build tasks is to leverage project time categories (A). Time categories classify the nature of work logged on time cards, enabling cost accounting systems to identify which hours are capitalizable. Creating task flags (B) or grouping tasks in a phase (C) are indirect workarounds. Creating an incident (D) is unrelated.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the default schedule for the Project Management application?

options.text: Repeats every week on weekdays Monday through Friday from 8:00am to noon and 1:00-5:00pm
Repeats every week on weekdays Monday through Friday
Repeats every week on weekdays Monday through Friday. Includes the child schedule U.S. Holidays
Repeats every week on weekdays Monday through Friday from 9:00am to 5:00pm

questions.explanation: The default schedule for the Project Management application repeats every week on weekdays Monday through Friday from 8:00am to noon and 1:00pm to 5:00pm (A). This standard 8-hour workday with a 1-hour lunch break is the OOB default schedule. Option B omits the time specification. Option C adds the U.S. Holidays child schedule. Option D uses 9am-5pm which differs from the default.

questions.stem: Demand managers can enhance a demand request by adding the following: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Three items demand managers can add to enhance a demand request are Requirements (A), Tasks (B), and Stakeholders (E). Per the docs: 'Demand managers can create as many requirements as needed' and 'When adding a stakeholder from the demand form...' Demand tasks (B) allow tracking demand-specific work. Expense lines (C) are financial records handled separately. Decisions (D) are RIDAC elements, not standard demand enhancement items.

questions.stem: To provide more meaningful information to senior management, you can view the FTE value under which of the following reports?
questions.explanation: FTE values can be viewed under Allocation Details (C) reports. Per the docs: 'Allocation details - A tabular breakdown of all allocation requests (soft bookings), committed allocations (hard bookings), availability, capacity, and actual hours.' Allocation Details provides a view rich enough to include FTE context for senior management. Resource Aggregate Reports (A) focus on capacity. Committed Utilization (D) is a ratio metric without FTE detail.

questions.stem: Which option should be used if you want to select the resource rate on the resource plan?
questions.explanation: Rate override (A) is used when selecting the resource rate directly on the resource plan. Per the docs: 'The hourly rate is derived from: Resource rate from the resource plan, if the Rate Override option is selected.' Rate override lets the PM specify a custom rate at the resource plan level. Labor rate card (B) is a fallback in the rate hierarchy. Rate model (C) is a structured rate configuration. Planned cost (D) is a calculated output, not a rate selector.

questions.stem: Which of the following tasks can be performed when innovation Management is integrated with Universal Request? (Choose two.)

options.text: Transfer an idea to another department
Create a project from a universal request
Send a universal request to a demand manager for review
Create an idea from a universal request

questions.explanation: Two tasks when Innovation Management is integrated with Universal Request are: Transfer an idea to another department (A) and Create an idea from a universal request (D). Per the docs, and -, the integration enables creating ideas from Universal Request tickets and transferring ideas between departments. Creating a project from UR (B) and sending UR to demand manager (C) are not specific capabilities of this integration.

questions.stem: The RIDAC workflow can be modified by using which recommended feature?
questions.explanation: The RIDAC workflow is best modified using Flow Designer (C). Flow Designer is the recommended modern tool in ServiceNow for modifying and extending workflows, including RIDAC processes. Workflow Editor (D) is the legacy tool and not recommended for new modifications. Service Catalog (A) and Project Form (B) are unrelated to RIDAC workflow modification.

questions.stem: A project status report can be viewed from which of the following areas? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: A project status report can be viewed from four areas: Project workspace (B), Project status form (C), Project record (E), and Portfolio workbench (F). Per the docs: viewing options include Project workspace, Project record, and Project Status form. The Portfolio workbench also surfaces project status reports. Program record (A) does not display project status reports. Planning console (D) is for task scheduling.

questions.stem: Which role is required to define custom schedules?
questions.explanation: The system admin (C) role is required to define custom schedules. Custom work schedules are system-level configurations that control when resources are available and how project task durations are calculated. resource_manager (A) manages resource allocation, pps_resource (B) is a basic resource role, and resource_user (D) has even less access.

questions.stem: As an administrator, what can you use to customize the PPM Mobile application?
questions.explanation: As an administrator, Mobile Studio (A) is used to customize the PPM Mobile application. Mobile Studio is ServiceNow's tool for building and customizing mobile app experiences. Now Platform App Engine (B) is for building applications generally. Now Mobile App (C) is the end-user app. Service Catalog (D) is for request management.

questions.stem: What are the three default project template configuration records available in the Template Config module? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Three default project template configuration records in the Template Config module are: Project subtask (A), Project task (B), and Project (D). Per the docs, the default template configuration includes the project root (pm_project = Project), project tasks, and project subtasks as the standard template hierarchy. Portfolio task (C), Program task (E), and Task (F) are not included.

questions.stem: If a sub-project and parent project have different project currencies, this property should be set to true for cost roll-ups.
questions.explanation: The property com.snc.project.multicurrency.rollup_if_different (A) should be set to true for cost roll-ups when a sub-project and parent project have different project currencies. Per the docs, this property controls whether costs roll up across projects with mismatched currencies. The other properties (B, C, D) control start date rollup, attribute copying, and ROI calculation respectively.

questions.stem: Can an it_project_manager convert a task to a milestone?

options.text: Yes, if the task is assigned to the project manager.
Yes, by right-clicking on the task in the Planning Console.
No, the PPS admin role is also required.
No, this can only be done by a system admin.

questions.explanation: Yes, an it_project_manager can convert a task to a milestone by right-clicking on the task in the Planning Console (B). Per the docs: 'You can also convert a task to milestone through Planning console tasks.' The conversion sets Duration to 0 making it a diamond milestone. PPS Admin (C) or system admin (D) roles are not required for this action.

questions.stem: Transition, Mobilize, Prepare and Conduct are included in which stage of the Now Create methodology?
questions.explanation: Transition, Mobilize, Prepare, and Conduct are phases included in the Prepare stage (D) of the Now Create methodology. The Now Create project delivery methodology organizes these four phases under the Prepare stage, which covers readiness activities before implementation begins. Initiate (C) is an earlier stage and Close (B) is the final stage.
